title: The Fall
definition: The Fall is humanity's rebellion against God through Adam's sin, bringing guilt, corruption, death, and brokenness into the world.
summary: The Fall explains why humanity and creation are corrupted by sin and death.
christFocus: Jesus is the promised Redeemer who comes to undo the curse of the Fall and restore what sin has ruined.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Fall refers to humanity's first rebellion against God. Adam and Eve distrusted God's Word, disobeyed His command, and brought sin, shame, death, alienation, and disorder into human life.

The Fall explains why the world is both beautiful and broken. Human relationships, desires, bodies, work, creation, and worship are all affected by sin.

Yet Genesis 3 also includes hope. God promises that the offspring of the woman will crush the serpent. Christ comes as the Redeemer who conquers sin, death, and the devil.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without the Fall, people either deny evil or blame God for human rebellion. This doctrine matters because it explains the depth of brokenness while pointing to God's promise of redemption.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Be honest about sin and brokenness without despairing. Do not normalize what the Fall has corrupted. Look to Christ as the Redeemer who restores and will one day make all things new.
